key_insight: The paper shows that LLM-written trapped-ion control code can be used safely by enforcing a hard authorization boundary: every hardware-reaching operation must carry a token tied to its exact contents.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical pattern for autonomous quantum-lab control, combining agent flexibility with per-operation safety gating for real hardware experiments.
method: LLM agent writes native ARTIQ control code through an MCP server
Each tool call is validated by exact-content authorization tokens
Tokens are issued by simulation-based checks (dax.sim) or human approval for sensitive actions
evidence_signal: The system is demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform where the agent autonomously builds a calibration stack, closes a magnetic-field-stabilization loop with operator help, and is also tested on a second ion platform for portability.
watch_item: Safety depends on the completeness of the token checks and simulation bounds, so adversarial bypass attempts reveal that the protection boundary still needs strengthening.
paper_title: A hardware-safety-gated system for LLM-written native ARTIQ control code on a trapped-ion platform
